reflection.text:
Unblinding: etoposide, PubChem CID 36462, ChEMBL DNA topoisomerase II inhibitor (name and BBBC021 structure agree, e15/e18). This correctly maps to truth MoA DNA damage in this atlas. Etoposide is a topoisomerase II poison/inhibitor that induces DNA damage PMID 16101488, PMID 42442624, PMID 35578785, so the DNA damage call is correct; verdict approve correct=true with p=0.66 was appropriately hedged not overconfident.

What evidence got right:

Dose ladder acquisition choice was discriminating. From list_available 8 doses 0.01-30uM, we sampled 0.3, 1, 3, 10uM (e3,e4,e5,e2) leaving 4 wells unused. This captured onset to Emax: at 0.3uM subtle - nuc_dna_mean z=-4.4 diluted by swelling but cell_major_axis z=+4.2, cell_area z=+3.7 (e3); at 1uM frac_large_nucleus z=+18.6, nuc_area z=+12.2, nuc_dna_integrated z=+7.4 (e4); at 3uM peak nuc_area z=+26.8, frac_large_nucleus z=+20.5, nuc_dna_integrated z=+19.5 (e5) with 494 cells; at 10uM still massive nuc_area z=+18.1, integrated DNA z=+10.8 (e2) with 406 cells. Coherent increases in nuclear size, large-nucleus fraction and integrated DNA across hundreds of cells per well argued for G2 arrest / accumulation of DNA content without cytoskeletal collapse, against microtubule/actin classes.

Comparison to reference atlas was decisive. NSC vote 4/4 DNA damage on those 4 wells (e6) with similarities 0.41-0.74 cited in rationale - unanimous 1-NN despite small n. The next-experiment rationale correctly prioritized orthogonal DNA damage readouts (gamma-H2AX, p53/p21, PI cell cycle) rather than more imaging.

Key Aurora discriminator was correctly used. e12 dose_response frac_multinucleate_proxy rho=+0.80 p=0.2 but absolute z=-1.77 to -0.31 never elevated across all 4 doses, and density similar vs DMSO at both 3uM (e7, 8 observations) and 0.3uM (e8, 5 observations). No frank multinucleation/polyploid morphology expected for Aurora inhibition, despite shared nuclear enlargement. This prevented flipping to Aurora despite pressure.

What misled / was ambiguous:

 e6 k-neighbour top-10 pooled: Aurora 7/10 vs DNA damage 3/10. Lower-similarity neighbours diluted the clean NSC signal, likely driven by shared large-nucleus phenotype between Aurora and DNA damage.

 e7 microscopist on 4 fields at 3uM labelled candidates Aurora kinase inhibitors despite describing uniform round single enlarged nuclei (per review) without multinucleation. We weighted this as supporting Aurora 0.24 in hypothesis update e13 but correctly listed e7 as contradicting DNA damage and e6/e12 as contradicting Aurora, so final weighting DNA damage 0.66 > Aurora 0.24 was justified.

 Dose_response statistics were underpowered and slightly inconsistent, which could mislead if over-interpreted: nuc_area rho=+0.80 p=0.2 e9, integrated DNA rho=+0.80 p=0.2 e10, frac_large_nucleus rho=+0.40 p=0.6 e11 - all non-significant with n=4 wells and single replicate per dose. Absolute effect sizes (z>10) were more informative than p-values. Non-monotonic drop from z=+26.8 at 3uM to +18.1 at 10uM (e5 to e2) also weakened rho but did not contradict DNA damage; could reflect plateau/toxicity.

What we missed / limits of acquisition:

 Only 4/8 doses sampled, all rep1 only (e1). We missed 0.01, 0.03, 0.1uM onset and 30uM high-toxicity point, and had no replicate to estimate variance beyond per-cell counts (330-603 cells). This left dose_response p-values uninterpretable and hedging at 0.66 appropriate.

 Literature search strategy was inefficient: e16 'etoposide topoisomerase' returned 629 hits/5 returned useful, but e17 'DNA damage induced nuclear enlargement G2 phenotype' returned 0 hits - overly specific query gave no support for enlarged-nuclei G2 interpretation, so we relied on atlas + microscopy.

 We did not acquire orthogonal DNA damage markers within the session; proposal was deferred to real-lab follow-up. Given Aurora vs DNA damage phenotypic overlap on size alone, a single gamma-H2AX acquisition would have been higher value than 4th size-related dose_response (e11).

Lesson: massive, coherent z-scores for nuc_area/integrated DNA/large-nucleus at multiple doses plus absent multinucleate proxy and unanimous NSC outweighs mixed k-neighbour vote and single microscopist label when the latter's own morphology description contradicts Aurora. Future runs should keep ladder design but include replicate at peak dose and one orthogonal DNA damage readout instead of redundant size correlations.
